record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Dynamics of Quadratic and Higher Degree Polynomial ODE Systems
record.original_question: Give a universal definition of non-chaotic solutions for continuous autonomous dynamical systems x' = f(x) on R^N. The definition should cover non-chaotic behavior beyond the authors' criterion that excludes bounded chaos when N-2 components of every solution eventually either tend to a finite limit, are periodic or asymptotic to a periodic function, are unbounded, or exhibit one of several finite-time behaviors; in particular, it should still work for N > 3, where that criterion remains unverified and incomplete.

evidence.quote: 3.2. Second Open Problem ... Giving a universal definition of non-chaotic solutions is another way to define chaotic solutions. It is known that it is also very difficult. In [Heidel & Zhang, 2007] we gave a conjecture on the criterion recognizing non-chaotic behavior: Consider the autonomous system x0 = f (x), x ∈ RN , t ∈ [0, ∞) ... Criterion 3.1. An N dimensional system (3.22) with no cluster points in the set of isolated fixed points has no bounded chaos if for any of its solutions there are N - 2 components ...

When N = 3 this criterion has been widely accepted. For N > 3 it still needs verification. Even if this criterion is very useful, it misses countless types of non–chaotic solutions. This open problem is to give a universal definition of non–chaotic solutions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider continuous autonomous dynamical systems
    x'(t) = f(x(t)),    x ∈ ℝ^N,  t ∈ [0, ∞),
where f : ℝ^N → ℝ^N is continuous (so that solutions exist for t ∈ [0, ∞)). Informally, a solution x(t) is called "chaotic" if it exhibits sensitive dependence on initial conditions and complicated long-term behavior, while a "non-chaotic" solution is any solution that does not display such behavior.

A known partial criterion for non-chaoticity reads as follows. Suppose the system has no cluster points in its set of isolated fixed points. Then the system has no bounded chaos provided that, for every solution, at least N − 2 of its components x_{i_1}(t), …, x_{i_{N−2}}(t) eventually satisfy at least one of the following:
 (i) tend to a finite limit as t → ∞;
 (ii) are periodic or asymptotic to a periodic function;
 (iii) are unbounded; or
 (iv) exhibit one of certain prescribed finite-time behaviors (e.g., blow-up in finite time, finite-time termination, or oscillations of unbounded frequency on a finite interval).
This criterion is widely accepted for N = 3 but remains unverified for N > 3, and even when valid it fails to capture many forms of non-chaotic behavior.

Problem. Formulate a universal definition of "non-chaotic solution" for the system x' = f(x) on ℝ^N, valid for every dimension N (in particular for N > 3), that:
 (a) reduces to or is consistent with the accepted notion of non-chaoticity in dimension N = 3;
 (b) encompasses every solution covered by the criterion above as a special case;
 (c) also includes the broad classes of non-chaotic solutions that the above criterion fails to detect; and
 (d) is intrinsic, i.e., expressible purely in terms of the qualitative dynamics of x(t) (such as its ω-limit set, recurrence structure, entropy, or sensitivity properties) without reference to the particular form of f.

Equivalently, provide a precise mathematical definition of non-chaoticity that, taken as the negation of "chaotic," yields a workable universal notion of chaotic solution for continuous autonomous ODE systems on ℝ^N.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of giving a universal definition of non-chaotic (equivalently, chaotic) solutions for continuous autonomous ODE systems on ℝ^N is widely recognized as an open conceptual problem in dynamical systems. The Heidel–Zhang criterion is established for N = 3 but not verified for N > 3, and even there it misses many non-chaotic behaviors. No accepted universal definition has been published; the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems in chaos theory and dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Giving a universal definition of non-chaotic solutions is another way to define chaotic solutions. ... For N > 3 it still needs verification. Even if this criterion is very useful, it misses countless types of non-chaotic solutions.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of providing a universal definition of non-chaotic solutions is explicitly stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Non-chaotic behaviour in three-dimensional quadratic systems (Heidel & Zhang)
status_evidence.snippet: Heidel and Zhang's criterion for non-chaotic behavior in 3D quadratic autonomous systems.
status_evidence.claim: The known criterion is for N = 3; the universal-N definition is not provided.
